problem: VLN agents such as DUET and HAMT are trained to act autonomously and have no way to signal that an under-specified instruction lacks the information needed for the next move. Prior uncertainty estimators each fail in one direction. ULN's navigator-attention/likelihood classifier and the VDN entropy estimator are overly confident (high precision, low recall). Conformal prediction (KnowNo) is overly cautious and asks at almost every step.
motivation: Real users give instructions of varied quality. DUET and HAMT trained on fine-grained R2R instructions degrade on the coarse ULN instructions: DUET SPL drops from 54.46 to 47.35 and HAMT from 43.82 to 31.58. An agent that asks for help at the right moments avoids detours and failures without pestering the human. The authors argue that vagueness is not a property of the instruction text alone (as ULN's instruction classifier assumes). It arises from how the instruction relates to the path and environment, so instruction-to-path alignment should be the signal.
key_idea: Attach a small, separately trained multi-head-attention module to a frozen VLN navigator. It attends from the instruction to the path so far plus the navigator's proposed next node and classifies each step as certain or uncertain (ask the oracle). The attention is optionally pretrained on FGR2R sub-instruction-to-path alignment, and supervision can use alignment-based pseudo-labels.
insight: An explicit instruction-to-path attention is a better vagueness signal than the navigator's own cross-modal attention and action likelihoods. With the same GP labels on DUET, f_IV(GP) beats f_Base (SPL 57.86 vs 52.10, balance 0.6220 vs 0.7319); on HAMT balance is 0.0652 vs 0.1324. Entropy-based labels (f_VDN) are unreliable because HAMT makes errors with high confidence, giving HAMT SPL 38.38 and balance 0.6731. Alignment-derived labels (label_IP) give near-perfect precision-recall balance on DUET: -0.0194 vs 0.6220 with label_GP, SPL 75.24. They also make the module instruction-style-aware (79% of short vs 26% of orig episodes get interventions). Since label_IP is unavailable for new data, pretraining the MHA on FGR2R alignment is the practical alternative. It improves the GP-trained module on both navigators: DUET SPL 57.86→58.10, NE 3.51→3.31; HAMT SPL 68.82→75.84, balance 0.0652→-0.0629.
method: Frozen navigator (VLN-DUET or HAMT): text encoder f_text gives instruction encoding Î; cross-attention gives graph-aware node features and visual-on-language attention α_t; action predictor gives node likelihoods β_t. No part of the navigator is retrained.

IV estimation module f_IV: appends the navigator's top-scoring next node to the path so far to form P̄_t. An 8-head MultiHead(Q=Î, K=V=P̄_t) with d_k=768 produces Instr_Path_Attn_t, and a linear 2-way classifier (certain/uncertain) runs on it. 'Uncertain' triggers a help request.
Oracle assistance: when help is requested, an oracle substitutes the shortest-path optimal next move for the navigator's prediction (a simulated human).

Pseudo-labels: label_GP marks a step uncertain if the predicted move differs from the ground-truth move. label_IP marks it uncertain if the FGR2R sub-instruction aligned with the current GT node is absent from the input instruction. Both are trained with BCE.

Pretraining task, Relevant Instruction Span Identification: an MHA + BiLSTM tags each instruction token as relevant or not for the move at step t. It is trained on FGR2R sub-instruction-to-node alignments with the navigator frozen and teacher-forced along the GT path, using equal-weight BCE + Dice loss. The MHA weights then initialize f_IV.
Training details: pretraining runs 7000 iterations with batch 8 and lr 1e-4. f_IV runs 1000 iterations with batch 8, lr 1e-4 and AdamW on a single RTX 4090.
Evaluation: step-level Balance = (P−R)/(P+R) in [-1,1] (0 means P=R), computed against label_GP, plus oracle-assisted SPL/NE.

setting.backbone: Frozen R2R-trained navigators VLN-DUET and HAMT, plus a small trained IV module (8-head MHA + linear classifier; MHA optionally pretrained with a BiLSTM head)
setting.training_data: Pretraining: R2R train split (~11,400 trajectories, 80/20 train/val) with FGR2R sub-instruction-to-path alignments. IV training: ~2,000 trajectories from ULN/R2R val_seen, 50% with original fine-grained instructions and 50% with ULN short (high-level) instructions.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB features as used by DUET/HAMT (DUET additionally uses object features), with a topological graph of visited/navigable nodes
setting.privileged: When the IV module requests help, an oracle provides the ground-truth shortest-path next move. Reported SPL/NE include these oracle interventions. The Balance metric is computed against GT-path-derived labels.

numbers.extra: Oracle gives the optimal move when help is requested. Test set: R2R val_unseen trajectories with 50% original (I_orig) and 50% ULN short (I_short) instructions. MHA pretrained on FGR2R alignment; IV trained on ~2k val_seen trajectories with label_GP.

numbers_note: All SPL/NE numbers are with oracle help at the steps flagged uncertain. They are not comparable to standard R2R results; e.g. the always-asking conformal baseline reaches 96.40 SPL. The evaluation set is R2R val_unseen with ULN's short instruction used for half the trajectories. The DUET-only table and the combined Table 2 share the same label and duplicate numbers. Some printed F-scores do not match the printed P/R (e.g., DUET f_IV(IP) P=37.5680, R=39.0566 gives F≈38.3, but 39.2978 is printed); values are copied as printed. The f_IV(GP) variant (DUET SPL 57.86/NE 3.51/Balance 0.6220; HAMT 68.82/3.21/0.0652) is omitted from entries. The number of oracle interventions per trajectory is shown only in a figure. The unassisted navigators (Table 1) score DUET SPL 54.46 (orig) / 47.35 (short) and HAMT 43.82 / 31.58.
results: With oracle assistance on mixed-style ULN val_unseen, f_IV(IP) on DUET reaches SPL 75.24 / NE 2.16 with near-perfect precision-recall balance (-0.0194). The ULN-style baseline f_Base gets 52.10 / 4.04 with balance 0.7319, and unassisted DUET on short instructions gets 47.35 SPL. On HAMT, the practical f_IV(GP+pretrain) reaches SPL 75.84 / NE 2.32 with balance -0.0629, beating f_Base (67.29 / 3.34, 0.1324) and f_VDN (38.38 / 5.63). Conformal prediction (f_CP) gets the highest SPL (96.40 on DUET) only because it asks at essentially every step (balance -0.4615).
limitations: Help is an oracle giving the shortest-path move rather than a real human or dialogue. The method only detects 'when' information is missing, not 'what' is missing.

Very small training data: ~2,000 val_seen trajectories for IV. label_IP needs sub-instruction alignment annotations, which are unavailable for new data. Evaluation covers only the discrete R2R/ULN val_unseen with two navigators.

SPL/NE gains are driven by oracle interventions, and the Balance metric ignores the number or cost of questions. Comparisons therefore mix estimator quality with how often each method asks (e.g., IV(GP+pretrain) on HAMT intervenes in 90-96% of episodes).
compares_to: VDN self-motivated entropy-based uncertainty estimator (f_VDN, Zhu et al. 2021)
